known_facts: VERIFIED (Commander-fetched 2026-08-29, https://www.ebmud.com/about-us/news/press-releases/ebmud-approves-8-percent-drought-surcharge): EBMUD board approved 8% drought surcharge May 10 2022 (6-1 vote), effective July 1 2022, applies to FLOW charges (volume of water used), Stage 2 drought emergency (declared April 26 2022, mandated 10% conservation district-wide vs 2020). Average single-family at 200 gal/day: ~10 cents/day, $3.08/month, $6.16/two-month cycle. Raises ~$30.8M/yr toward $64.5M drought costs (rest from reserves). Stays until drought emergency declaration lifted. Excessive Use Penalty: threshold 66 CCF/month (~1,646 gal/day), fines $2 per 748 gallons above after one warning. Prior surcharge 25% July 1 2015–June 30 2016. Stage ladder max surcharges: Stage 1 0%, Stage 2 8%, Stage 3 20%, Stage 4 25%. HISTORICAL — lifted when drought ended; label as such.

VERIFIED (Commander-fetched 2026-08-29, https://www.saws.org/service/water-sewer-rates/high-use-drought-surcharge/): San Antonio Water System high-use drought surcharge $10.37 per 1,000 gallons, effective for consumption on/after July 6 2024, residential + billed commercial irrigation. Stage 3 trigger: residential use above 20,000 gal/month; Stage 4: above 12,000 gal/month. SAWS's own worked example: Stage 3 customer using 25,000 gal owes 5 × $10.37 = $51.85. Purpose: push biggest users to cut during advanced drought stages.

VERIFIED (Commander-fetched 2026-08-29, https://www.lvvwd.com/customer-service/pay-bill/euc-faq.html): Las Vegas Valley Water District Excessive Use Charge (EUC) $9 per 1,000 gallons above seasonal thresholds (30-day billing period): winter ~14,000 gal (Nov 1), spring ~16,000 (Mar 1), summer ~28,000 (May 1), fall ~26,000 (Sept 1); thresholds scale with billing-period length (28-day summer cycle = 26,000; 33-day = 31,000). Annual allowance 252,000 gal. Affects roughly top 10% of residential users; thresholds set at more than 2× median seasonal use; >50% of charged customers got it only once or twice. ONGOING structure — not tied to a declared stage ending.

Context (search-verified 2026-08-29, austintexas.gov/water/austin-water-drought-response): Austin returned to Conservation Stage (no surcharge) as of Sept 2 2025 after Stage 2 — useful FAQ counter-example: not every conservation stage carries a surcharge.
